title: Game capability
description: One game's answer to one shared capability: the exact mechanism, its preconditions, and the evidence establishing both. The shared `capability` id is navigation; everything under `mechanism` is the evidence a creator's implementation actually rests on.

capability.description: An id from the shared taxonomy in modcheck.capabilities.

mechanism.description: The exact extension point. This is what an implementation is written against, so it must be specific enough to write code from. Uses the shared `target` definition -- the same vocabulary recipes, findings and interactions already use, so an exact target means the same thing everywhere in the system.

requirements.description: What must already be true. A precondition is not advice; if it does not hold, the mechanism does not work.

ordering.description: Lifecycle, threading, authority or load-order rules that govern when this may be used.

limits.description: What this mechanism cannot do, stated so a plan does not quietly assume it can.

validation.description: How a creator confirms the capability actually works in their project, and what that check does NOT establish.

recipes.description: Recipes in this pack that implement this capability.

evidence_state.description: What the references establish. `documented` is an intent statement; `source_confirmed` means the framework's own source or an installed toolchain definition was read; `example_confirmed` means a working project was read; `build_tested` means our own build ran; `game_tested` requires a real game run and may not be claimed otherwise.

invalidated_by.description: What would make this record wrong: a version bump, an API removal, a toolchain change.

runs_on.description: Which side this mechanism executes on. Structured rather than left to prose in `limits`, because it is the commonest source of a requirement conflict: a value held server-side cannot be read by a client-side display without a synchronisation step, and a plan that does not notice compiles fine and shows nothing.

scope.description: What one instance of this mechanism attaches to. Structured because capability alone is too coarse: world-scoped and per-object persistence are both `persist_state`, and a plan that cannot tell them apart will happily select a single world value for a requirement about many objects. The resulting code compiles and every object reads the same number.
